title: Only 1 in 10 facilities met the standard
plain_language: Just 280 of 2,583 facilities (10.8%) scored the 80% needed to meet the maternal & child health quality standard.
so_what: Most local clinics fall short across the board. Access alone doesn't guarantee good care.

title: Maternal death reviews were the bright spot
plain_language: Maternal death reviews (MPDSR) were the most-implemented indicator, done by 2,057 facilities (79.6%).
so_what: Facilities can follow a guideline when it's prioritised, but a review only helps if someone acts on it.

title: Cervical cancer screening is barely offered
plain_language: Only 199 facilities (7.7%) offered cervical cancer screening, the lowest of all 12 indicators.
so_what: A largely preventable cancer goes unscreened in most clinics, against the WHO 2030 elimination goal.

title: Emergency obstetric supplies are often missing
plain_language: Key obstetric medicines and supplies were available in just 424 facilities (16.4%).
so_what: Life-saving supplies are absent exactly where childbirth emergencies must be managed.

title: Newborn care space is rare
plain_language: Among 394 hospitals and health centres, only 60 (15.2%) had postnatal and newborn care with dedicated neonatal and KMC space.
so_what: Sick and small newborns often have nowhere equipped to be cared for.

title: Higher-level facilities do far better
plain_language: Compared with dispensaries, health centres were about 7 times more likely to meet the standard (AOR 7.21) and hospitals about 35 times (AOR 34.7).
so_what: Quality concentrates at the higher levels. Dispensaries, where most people go first, lag furthest behind.

title: Public facilities outperform private
plain_language: Public facilities were about three times as likely to meet the standard as private ones (AOR 2.94, 95% CI 1.80–5.05).
so_what: Free government MCH services may drive investment that private, cost-driven clinics lack.

title: Enough nurses matters
plain_language: Facilities with sufficient nurse staffing were about twice as likely to meet the standard (AOR 2.12, 95% CI 1.34–3.53); clinician numbers showed no significant effect.
so_what: Nurses, not doctors, carry much of the quality here, so staffing them is one of the clearest fixes.

title: Functional teams lift quality
plain_language: Functional Health Facility Management Teams (AOR 1.62) and Quality Improvement Teams (AOR 1.71) both predicted meeting the standard, yet only 560 of 2,358 facilities (24%) had a functional QIT.
so_what: Leadership and quality-improvement teams are cheap to set up, yet most facilities still don't have them.

title: Urban vs rural made no real difference
plain_language: After adjustment, urban facilities were no more likely to meet the standard than rural ones (AOR 1.07, 95% CI 0.69–1.62; p = 0.75).
so_what: The quality gap comes down to facility level, ownership and management, not simply town versus countryside.
